title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 17-18
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 17 to 18 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'उपेन्द्रो वामनः प्रांशुरमोघः शुचिरूर्जितः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 17 to 18 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 17 to 18.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 17 to 18** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **उपेन्द्रो वामनः प्रांशुरमोघः शुचिरूर्जितः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**उपेन्द्रो वामनः प्रांशुरमोघः शुचिरूर्जितः । अतीन्द्रः सङ्ग्रहः सर्गो धृतात्मा नियमो यमः ॥** **वेद्यो वैद्यः सदायोगी वीरहा माधवो मधुः । अतीन्द्रियो महामायो महोत्साहो महाबलः ॥**

He came as Vamana, the younger brother of Indra. Tall, pure and mighty is that God of gods. Beyond Indra himself, he shapes creation and holds everyone within order. He is the one to be known, the healer, ever steady in yoga. Madhava, who slew Madhu, is that God of gods. Beyond the senses, of great maya, great zeal and great strength is he.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 17 to 18 mean?
faq.a: He came as Vamana, the younger brother of Indra. Tall, pure and mighty is that God of gods. Beyond Indra himself, he shapes creation and holds everyone within order. He is the one to be known, the healer, ever steady in yoga. Madhava, who slew Madhu, is that God of gods. Beyond the senses, of great maya, great zeal and great strength is he.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
